Alabama.filing_fee: roughly $35–$198 state base (counties add local fees)
Alabama.waiting_period: 3 years after misdemeanor conviction; 2-year clean record for dismissed charges
Alabama.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted charges; nonviolent misdemeanor, municipal, and minor traffic convictions

Alaska.what_qualifies: sealing only for mistaken identity or false accusation

Arizona.lawyer_allowed: no — attorneys may not appear in small claims
Arizona.waiting_period: 2–10 years depending on offense (30 days for non-convictions)
Arizona.what_qualifies: misdemeanors and most felonies; non-conviction records; certain marijuana offenses

Arkansas.lawyer_allowed: no — hiring one moves the case to regular civil division
Arkansas.waiting_period: none for misdemeanors and nonviolent C/D felonies; 5 years for violent C/D felonies
Arkansas.what_qualifies: non-conviction records; most misdemeanors; nonviolent Class C/D felonies and some drug felonies

California.available: yes — expungement (and automatic relief for many)
California.lawyer_allowed: no at the hearing — can advise beforehand; allowed on appeal
California.what_qualifies: convictions after probation complete; many non-conviction arrests and eligible low-level convictions cleared automatically

Colorado.lawyer_allowed: generally no — only if the other side also has one
Colorado.waiting_period: 1–5 years by petition; automatic sealing takes longer
Colorado.what_qualifies: non-conviction records; most misdemeanors and lower-level felonies

Connecticut.waiting_period: 7 years for misdemeanors, 10 years for Class D/E felonies (from most recent conviction)
Connecticut.what_qualifies: non-convictions; most misdemeanors; Class D/E felonies

Delaware.lawyer_allowed: yes — parties may appear on their own or with a lawyer
Delaware.waiting_period: 3–7 years depending on offense; none for non-convictions
Delaware.what_qualifies: non-conviction records; misdemeanors; single non-violent felony (must show manifest injustice)

Florida.waiting_period: none — apply once eligible (FDLE certificate required)
Florida.what_qualifies: dismissed, dropped, or acquitted charges; eligible withheld-adjudication offenses may be sealed

Georgia.filing_fee: typically $50–$100 (varies by county and claim size)
Georgia.waiting_period: 4 years after misdemeanor sentence complete; none for non-convictions
Georgia.what_qualifies: non-conviction arrests; up to two misdemeanor convictions; felonies only after pardon

Hawaii.max_claim: $5,000 (no limit for residential security deposit cases)
Hawaii.waiting_period: 1 year after discharge for deferred pleas; varies by offense
Hawaii.what_qualifies: arrests not charged or dismissed, acquittals, deferred pleas; some convictions under 2024 Clean Slate law

Idaho.what_qualifies: arrests not charged, acquittals, dismissed cases (not convictions)

Illinois.filing_fee: about $89–$264 depending on county and claim size
Illinois.waiting_period: none for acquittals/dismissals; 2–3 years for sealing; 5 years for certain probation
Illinois.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted cases can be expunged; most convictions can be sealed

Indiana.waiting_period: 1 year for arrests; 5 years for misdemeanors; 8–10 years for felonies
Indiana.what_qualifies: most arrests, misdemeanors, and many felonies (not sex or violent offenses)

Iowa.waiting_period: 180 days for acquittals/dismissals; 8 years for misdemeanor convictions
Iowa.what_qualifies: acquittals and dismissed charges; some misdemeanor convictions

Kansas.lawyer_allowed: generally no — only if the other side is represented
Kansas.waiting_period: 3 years for misdemeanors/minor felonies; 5 years for serious felonies and DUI
Kansas.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors, minor felonies, dismissed charges, diversions (not violent or sex offenses)

Kentucky.filing_fee: about $35–$75 depending on how the defendant is served
Kentucky.what_qualifies: misdemeanors, violations, and many Class D felonies; acquittals and dismissals

Louisiana.filing_fee: about $100–$160 depending on parish and court
Louisiana.waiting_period: 5 years for misdemeanors, 10 years for felonies, after sentence completion
Louisiana.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and non-violent felonies (not sex crimes or crimes of violence)

Maine.waiting_period: 4 years after sentence for eligible youthful offenses
Maine.what_qualifies: sealing for low-level Class E misdemeanors committed at ages 18–21

Maryland.waiting_period: none for acquittals/dismissals; 3 years for probation-before-judgment; 3–5 years for most convictions
Maryland.what_qualifies: acquittals/dismissals, probation-before-judgment, stet, pardons, and many misdemeanor and felony convictions

Michigan.what_qualifies: up to 3 felonies and unlimited misdemeanors (most nonviolent offenses)

Minnesota.lawyer_allowed: generally no, unless the judge allows it
Minnesota.what_qualifies: dismissed cases; misdemeanors, gross misdemeanors, and listed felonies; some automatic under Clean Slate

Mississippi.waiting_period: varies — immediate for non-convictions; up to 15 years for felonies
Mississippi.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted cases; first-offense misdemeanors; up to 3 felonies after 15 years

Missouri.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and non-Class-A felonies (violent/sex/DWI excluded)

Montana.available: very limited — no adult felony expungement
Montana.lawyer_allowed: no, unless all parties have one
Montana.what_qualifies: misdemeanors once per lifetime; dismissed deferred sentences

Nebraska.available: very limited — no expungement of adult convictions
Nebraska.waiting_period: varies — 1–3 years for sealing non-conviction records
Nebraska.what_qualifies: sealing for arrests/charges with no conviction; set-aside for probation/fine sentences

Nevada.lawyer_allowed: yes, but attorney's fees can't be awarded
Nevada.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and felonies; sex crimes/child crimes/felony DUI excluded

New Hampshire.what_qualifies: most violations, misdemeanors, and felonies except certain violent/sexual offenses

New Jersey.waiting_period: 5 years (most offenses); 10 years for automatic Clean Slate
New Jersey.what_qualifies: most indictable offenses (limited number), disorderly persons offenses, municipal ordinances

New Mexico.waiting_period: 1 year for non-convictions; 2–10 years for convictions by severity
New Mexico.what_qualifies: arrests without conviction; most misdemeanors and felonies after sentence is complete

New York.available: yes — Clean Slate automatic sealing (no true expungement except some cannabis cases)
New York.waiting_period: 3 years for misdemeanors, 8 years for felonies (automatic sealing)
New York.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies; arrests that did not lead to conviction are sealed

North Carolina.waiting_period: immediate for dismissals; 3 years for misdemeanors; 10 years for felonies
North Carolina.what_qualifies: dismissed charges and acquittals; nonviolent misdemeanors and felonies

North Dakota.available: yes — sealing (no true expungement of convictions)
North Dakota.waiting_period: 3 years crime-free for misdemeanors; 5 years for felonies
North Dakota.what_qualifies: nonviolent misdemeanors and felonies, with good cause and reformation shown

Ohio.waiting_period: 6 months–1 year for misdemeanors; 11–13 years for felonies
Ohio.what_qualifies: dismissals and acquittals; misdemeanors; 4th/5th-degree and some 3rd-degree felonies

Oklahoma.waiting_period: immediate for dismissals; 5 years for one nonviolent felony; 10 years for two
Oklahoma.what_qualifies: dismissals and acquittals; deferred sentences; nonviolent misdemeanors and felonies

Oregon.lawyer_allowed: generally no — only with the judge's approval
Oregon.what_qualifies: most misdemeanors and eligible felonies (no Class A, violent, or sex offenses)

Pennsylvania.available: yes — expungement for non-convictions; Clean Slate automatic sealing
Pennsylvania.filing_fee: unverified — varies by county and claim size
Pennsylvania.waiting_period: 5–10 years depending on offense (many records sealed automatically)
Pennsylvania.what_qualifies: non-convictions expunged; summary offenses and most misdemeanors sealed

Rhode Island.waiting_period: 5 years for misdemeanors; 10 years for felonies (15 for multiple felonies)
Rhode Island.what_qualifies: first-offender nonviolent misdemeanors and felonies; deferred sentences

South Carolina.waiting_period: immediate for dismissals; 3–5 years for convictions
South Carolina.what_qualifies: dismissed charges; first-offense misdemeanors; certain nonviolent felonies

South Dakota.available: very limited — no general expungement of adult convictions
South Dakota.waiting_period: 1 year after dismissal or no-charge arrest; automatic removal of minor offenses after about 5–10 years (sources vary)
South Dakota.what_qualifies: arrests never charged, dismissed charges, acquittals; petty/Class 2 misdemeanor offenses auto-removed after about 10 years

Tennessee.filing_fee: varies by county, roughly $120–$275 including service
Tennessee.waiting_period: none for dismissals/acquittals; 5 years after sentence completion for misdemeanors and Class E felonies, 10 years for eligible Class C/D and drug felonies
Tennessee.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted charges; eligible nonviolent misdemeanors and certain Class C–E felonies

Texas.filing_fee: varies by county, typically $35–$60 filing (service extra)
Texas.waiting_period: none for acquittals; 180 days–3 years by offense level for dismissals; 5 years after discharge for most felony nondisclosures
Texas.what_qualifies: acquitted or dismissed charges, pardons; deferred-adjudication cases get nondisclosure (sealing)

Utah.waiting_period: 3–10 years depending on offense class (3 yrs Class C misdemeanor, 4 yrs Class B, 5 yrs Class A/felony drug possession, 7 yrs most felonies, 10 yrs DUI)
Utah.what_qualifies: arrests without conviction; eligible misdemeanors and some nonviolent felonies within conviction-count limits

Vermont.max_claim: $10,000 ($5,000 for consumer credit and medical debt claims)
Vermont.waiting_period: 5 years after sentence completion for expungement; dismissed charges auto-sealed after about 60 days
Vermont.what_qualifies: qualifying nonviolent misdemeanors and some nonviolent felonies; dismissed charges sealed automatically

Virginia.available: yes — expungement for non-convictions, sealing for some convictions since 2025
Virginia.lawyer_allowed: generally no — self-represented (case moves to the regular docket if a lawyer appears)
Virginia.max_claim: $5,000 (small claims division of General District Court)
Virginia.waiting_period: none for dismissals/acquittals; 7 crime-free years for automatic sealing of eligible misdemeanors, 10 years for eligible felonies
Virginia.what_qualifies: dismissed/acquitted charges; since July 2025, certain misdemeanor and Class 5/6 felony convictions

Washington.lawyer_allowed: no, unless the judge gives permission
Washington.waiting_period: 3 years after sentence completion (misdemeanors), 5 years (Class C felonies), 10 years (Class B felonies)
Washington.what_qualifies: certain misdemeanors and Class B/C felonies; not DUI or most sex/violent offenses

West Virginia.available: yes — expungement of misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies
West Virginia.waiting_period: 1 year (single misdemeanor), 2 years (multiple misdemeanors), 5 years (nonviolent felony) after sentence/supervision ends
West Virginia.what_qualifies: misdemeanors and nonviolent felonies from the same transaction; excludes violent, sexual, DUI, and domestic-violence offenses

Wisconsin.waiting_period: no fixed waiting period — ordered at sentencing and takes effect after sentence completion
Wisconsin.what_qualifies: under 25 at the time of the offense, offense carries 6 years or less maximum imprisonment, ordered at sentencing

Wyoming.waiting_period: 180 days for arrest records; 5 years for misdemeanors; 10 years for felonies after sentence completion
Wyoming.what_qualifies: arrests never charged, dismissed charges, acquittals; eligible misdemeanor and nonviolent felony convictions
